source.publication: 2025 NJ-1040 Instructions (with GIT-1 & 2 Retirement Income, January 2026, and njit6/njit7 web pages where named)
source.section: Form NJ-1040 lines 15, 20a, 27, 28a, 29: Instr PDF p.15 line 20a ('Federal, state, and local government, and teachers' pensions' taxable), njit6 Taxable Retirement Income ('all state and local government ... pensions'), GIT-1 & 2 p.4, PDF p.22 line 28a (Line A, Line B and chart), PDF p.22 line 28b and PDF p.23 Worksheet D lines 1-9 with the Maximum Exclusion chart, PDF p.22 line 29 (line 27 of exactly $100,000 is in the $0-$100,000 column); PDF p.8 lines 6-7 (regular and senior 65+ exemptions), PDF p.9 line 13, PDF p.25 line 30, PDF p.27 lines 38-39, PDF p.33 lines 42-43, PDF p.65 Tax Rate Schedules

worked: Federal AGI 100,000.00 (spouse 1 New York State retirement system pension 60,000.00 + spouse 2 wages 40,000.00); federal taxable income = 100,000.00 - 31,500.00 federal standard deduction = 68,500.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). A New York State pension of a New Jersey resident is taxable like any other state's government pension (no reciprocity rule; New York does not tax it for a nonresident, so there is no credit for tax paid to another jurisdiction). Line 15 wages 40,000.00 + line 20a pension 60,000.00 = line 27 total income 100,000.00; measure 100,000.00, exactly 100,000.00, which is still the $0-$100,000 column (keep share 1). Line 28a: only spouse 1 (64) qualifies; Line A = his pension 60,000.00, Line B 100,000.00; lesser = 60,000.00. Line 28b: wages 40,000 over 3,000, so no unclaimed exclusion; projection 0.00 (no covered interest, dividends or gains). Line 29 New Jersey gross income = 100,000.00 - 60,000.00 - 0.00 = 40,000.00. Line 30 exemptions (line 13): regular 1,000 x 2 (nobody is 65 or older, so no senior exemption) = 2,000.00; line 38 = 2,000.00 (no other deductions). Line 39/42 taxable income = 40,000.00 - 2,000.00 = 38,000.00. Line 43 tax, rate schedule Table B (joint/head of household/qualifying widow(er)) as bands: 20,000.00 x 0.014 = 280.00 + 18,000.00 x 0.0175 = 315.00 = 595.00. The booklet's Tax Table (taxable income under 100,000) gives 595 for the 38,000-38,050 row (schedule at the midpoint 38,025, rounded); expected keeps the exact schedule result. No credits. State income tax = 595.00. The pension is treated as noncontributory (Tier 1-2 member), so line 20a equals the federal taxable amount. One dollar more of line 27 (100,001, the next chart column) would cut the exclusion to 50% x 60,000 = 30,000.
accepted_approximations: Tax Table: for taxable income under 100,000 New Jersey uses its Tax Table, the schedule's tax at each 50-dollar row's midpoint rounded to the dollar; the projection uses the exact schedule.
